articles.title: League Vacancy - Media Officer
articles.meta: Thu 29th October 2026 | Vacancies | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The North West Counties Football League (NWCFL) are seeking an ambitious and reliable individual to join the team as a Media Officer.

If you are looking to build a career in the media, digital marketing or social media, this role could be perfect for you. The League was an early adopter of social media and our website attracts over one million visitors during the football season.

We looking for someone to work as part of the team to assist in delivering the current media strategy for the League. This would be on the league website and across our social media platforms.

For full details including a role description please CLICK HERE or go to the League Vacancies section of this website.  Interested parties can also The League Media Manager Martin Fallon whose details are in the Contacts section of this website for an informal discussion about the role.

articles.title: September 2026 Player of the Month announced
articles.meta: Thu 5th November 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The Winners of the Player of the Month Awards for September 2026 have been announced by the NWCFL.

PREMIER DIVISION

The North West Counties League Premier Division Player of the Month Award for September 2026 has gone to Oliver Hodgson of Longridge Town.

Oliver came through at Burnley and made his debut in the NWCFL as a 16-year old at Nelson. After two seasons there he moved to Bacup Borough after two seasons to continue his development under Brent Peters. He was named Player of the Month in the First Division North in December 2025. This past summer he moved to Bury as part of their newly established Emerging Talent Group, and joined Longridge in August on a season long loan.

September was a phenomenal month for Oliver who played in all six games that his side played in the month. He scored in every single game, nothing up ten goals in total. He scored once in the games at Irlam and Charnock Richard as well as one in their home game with Glossop North End. He found the net twice in their game at Atherton LR, and also scored twice at AFC Liverpool to give his side a 2-1 win.

His best in the month though was scoring a hat-trick in his sides win at home to Abbey Hey, a game that also saw him named as Man of the Match by Abbey Hey due to his performance.

Congratulations Oliver!

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

The First Division North Player of the Month for September 2026 goes to Barney Wiggin of Colne.

Barney came through the ranks at FC Halifax Town before switching to Colne at the start of last season which is his first senior club. He soon established himself as a key member of the team and has really kicked on this season. This is the first time Barney has won this award.

September saw Barney play in all eight games that Colne played. He found the net in six of those games, scoring nine goals in total. He hit the only goal in the opening game against Bacup before scoring the second in a 2-0 win at Squires Gate. He also won Man of the Match in that game. The highlight of the month came as Colne thrashed Darwen 6-0, Barney getting a hat-trick as well as winning Man of the Match.

He scored in the 2-0 win at Tow Law Town in the FA Vase and then the equaliser at home to Holker Old Boys in a 1-1 draw. Barney picked up his third Man of the Match in that game also. He also found the net twice against Bamber Bridge in Colne's 4-3 loss in the Lancashire Trophy.

Congratulations to Barney on a fine month.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

The First Division South Player of the Month for September 2026 goes to forward Daniel Clarkson of Stafford Town.

Daniel came through the ranks at Chasetown and joined Stafford at the start of this season to help continue his development. He is certainly doing that if September is anything to go by!

His best position is deep lying midfielder, constantly breaking down opposition attacks and setting Stafford on their way forward. He did this excellently in the first two games of the month which enabled his team to record home victories over Allscott Heath and Alsager Town. Daniel was named as the opposition Man of the Match in both of these games, as well as grabbing an assist in each of them.

Daniel was also instrumental in the 3-3 draw at Cheadle Heath Nomads as Stafford twice came from behind to grab a point, claiming another assist for Staffords third goal of the afternoon.

Congratulations Daniel!

articles.title: October 2026 PST Sport Club of the Month
articles.meta: Thu 5th November 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
We are delighted to confirm our PST Sport Club of the Month winners for October 2026.

PST Sport are a recognised leader in artificial grass pitch construction, delivering complete turnkey solutions for both new build and resurfacing projects. From groundworks and drainage to subbase construction, surfacing, fencing, floodlighting and long-term maintenance, they offer a full-service approach that ensures clubs receive world-class playing surfaces tailored to their needs.

The league have a formula to work out our Club of the Month based on whether games were home and away and the quality of the opposition. Last months winners were are as follows:

Premier Division - Barnoldswick Town

Winning the Premier Division award for October 2026 is Barnoldswick Town. It has been a long wait for this award for Barlick, with the last time they won this award coming back in August 2021 in the first season following Covid-19.

After winning four of their six games in September, Barnoldswick took this form into October where they had a perfect month. Six games played with six victories, four of these coming in the Premier Division which saw them climb to second in the league, whilst they also progressed through to the next round of the Macron Cup and West Riding County Cup. They scored a whopping 24 goals and conceded just six, whilst they also registered two clean sheets.

The first game in October for Barnoldswick was at Irlam, last month's Club of the Month. It was a close game as expected, with Connor McAuley grabbing the only goal of the game midway through the second half. Next was a home game against Abbey Hey, with William Connor giving them an early lead after five minutes. It was still 1-0 in the 39th minute when Kuda Chingwaro went goal crazy, hitting a hat-trick inside six minutes to make it 4-1 at the break. Abbey Hey pulled one back at the start of the second half before Chingwaro grabbed his fourth on 56 minutes. Abbey grabbed another towards the end with 5-2 the final score.

Litherland REMYCA were their next visitors, with first half goals from Connor McAuley, William Procter and Kuda Chingwaro giving them a comfortable 3-0 lead at the break. REMYCA pulled one back ten minutes into the second half from the penalty spot, only for Procter to restore the three goal lead with a penalty of his own. REMYCA added another in stoppage time to make it 4-2.

The third game saw First Division North side Darwen visit in the Macron Cup with another quick start giving them a platform to build on. William Procter scored another penalty with Kuda Chingwaro adding the second with just 18 minutes on the clock. Ryan Bolton added the third and final goal on 77 minutes to put Barnoldswick through.

From opposition the league below to opposition the league above next, with Ossett United visiting in the West Riding County Cup. A fifth minute goal from Ryan Bolton put Barlick ahead only for Ossett to level midway through the half. Kuda Chingwaro restored the lead on the hour, before William Procter and Connor McAuley both scored in the last ten minutes to give their side a 4-2 win.

The final league game of the month was a trip to Glossop North End with Irlam running out 3-0 winners. Daniel Dolling opened the scoring on 11 minutes with Ross Davidson doubling the lead on the stroke of halftime. Dolling scored his second of the game five minutes from time to record a convincing win.

The last game of the month was their best performance with FC Isle of Man the visitors. Danylo Dmytriiev put them ahead after just three minutes before adding another just before the break. The second half saw Hamid Addai scored twice in the first eight minutes before Ryan Bolton made it five just after the hour. Kuda Chingwaro made it six with 20 minutes remaining, before Samuel Pickles completed the scoring with four minutes to go.

Burscough also had a strong month once again with five wins from five, with Prestwich Heys and Nelson both winning four games from five played.

Total Games played in the Month: 6Total Points won in the Month: 20Average: 3.33

First Division North - Fulwood Amateurs

Club of the Month in the First Division North is Fulwood Amateurs, who are winning one of the leagues monthly awards for the very first time since promotion to the league.

October saw them play seven games with five victories and one draw. They progressed in the Macron Cup with a win over Premier Division side Euxton Villa and the Edward Case Cup (on penalties), with their only loss coming at home to Northern League Division One side Yarn & Eaglescliffe in the FA Vase. They scored 18 goals in total and conceded just ten, with five of those coming in that Vase game.

The first game in October was at home to Daisy Hill with Spencer Lucas giving them the lead just after the half hour mark. It remained that way until five minutes from time with Lucas added his second, with Charlie Ridge adding the third and final goal in the last minute.

The next game saw Ashton Town visit in the Edward Case Cup. Arran Beattie gave them the lead on 24 minutes, and they were denied victory as Ashton levelled three minutes from time. That meant a penalty shoot out, with Longridge winning 4-2 from the spot.

Yarn & Eaglescliffe were next in the FA Vase, their opponents playing in the league above them at Step 5. A Tom Atkinson double gave Yarn a two goal lead at half time, with Spencer Lucas pulling one back on the hour. Two more goals for Yarn, including a hat-trick goal from Atikinson, made it four to put the game beyond Fulwood. Hugo Strand pulled one back in the last minute, with Yarn going down the other end to grab another in a 5-2 win.

Another Step 5 team were next as Premier Division Euxton Villa visited in the Macron Cup. Spencer Lucas gave them an early first half lead, with Euxton levelling in the first minute of the second half. Charlie Ridge restored the lead on the hour, with Spencer Lucas making it three ten minutes later. Will Sim made it 4-1 in the last minute to send Fulwood through.

Fulwood were back to league action on the final day of the month with a trip to Ashton Town. The home side led through a penalty just before the break, and it remained that way until five minutes from time when Matthew Van Wyk levelled. Spencer Lucas then hit the winner with a minute remaining.

Last month's winner Flixton had another good month with four wins and two draws, with Thornton Cleveleys having three wins and two draws.

Total Games played in the Month: 7Total Points won in the Month: 19Average: 2.71

First Division South - Barnton

The winner of the Club of the Month in the First Division South is Barnton. If Barnoldswick have been waiting a while to win one of these, then they have nothing on Barnton whose last won the Club of the Month almost 11 years ago in November 2015!

They played seven games in the month with six wins and one draw. They progressed in the Macron Cup with a win away at Premier Division side Irlam as well as progression in the Cheshire Senior Cup and Edward Case Cup. They scored 22 goals and conceded just seven.

The first game in October at Shawbury United. James Sigsworth opened the scoring just before the break and then added a second goal ten minutes into the second half. Shawbury pulled one back midway through the half before Bailey Sherlock made it 3-1 four minutes into the second half.

Eccleshall were next in the Edward Case Cup, with Barnton pulling out their best performance of the month. Charley Jarrald, Matthew Coughlan and Jack McKean gave them a three goal lead at the break with Ryan Eiselt starting the second half perfectly for them with the fourth just two minutes in. Callum Sandle made it five just after the hour with Joel Hind making it six with 20 minutes to go.

Back to league action next with Dawley Town the visitors. The visitors raced into a two goal lead with James Sigsworth starting the comeback by pulling one back in the first half. Thomas Stanton then levelled midway through the second half before Charley Jarrald put Barnton ahead for the first time with 12 minutes to go. They saw out the remaining time to win 3-2.

Barnton made it six successive wins in the next game, a 2-0 success against Cammell Laird 1907 in the Cheshire Senior Cup. Matthew Coughlan put them ahead on 28 minutes with Callum Sandle adding the second five minutes before half time.

Their only dropped points in the month came in a thrilling 3-3 draw at home to AFC Bridgnorth. It was the visitors who raced into a two goal lead only for Matthew Coughlan and Callum Sandle to pull the scores level by half time. Harry Watson then put Barnton ahead for the first time on 68 minutes only for the visitors to make it three each just two minutes later.

A trip to Irlam in the Macron Cup was then postponed due to Storm Boelo, with the game quickly arranged for three nights later. That saw Toby Humphries put them ahead with his first goal since August, only for Irlam to level 20 minutes into the second half. With penalties looming, Harry Watson then put Barnton back in front with three minutes to go before James Sigsworth confirmed a 3-1 win in stoppage time.

The final game was on Saturday with a trip to Foley Meir. Toby Humphries put them ahead just before the half hour with Thomas Stanton doubling the lead six minutes into the second half. There were no further goals with Barnton winning 2-0.

Barnton edged out Wolverhampton Casuals who had five wins and one loss from their six games. Others doing well included AFC Bridgnorth who had five wins and two draws from their eight games, with Bilston Town having four wins and a draw from their six games.

Total Games played in the Month: 7Total Points won in the Month: 24Average: 3.43

Congratulations to all of the winners.

articles.title: FA Vase Third Round Proper Draw
articles.meta: Mon 2nd November 2026 | FA Challenge Vase | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The FA have today released the draw details for the Third Round Proper of the 2026/27 FA Vase.

Sixty of our member Clubs have entered this year's competition and six will be playing in this round after wins on Saturday. Once again all six have the opportunity to progress through to the next round as they avoided each other in the draw, and strangely all six have been given home ties.

Woolton have reached the Third Round of the Vase for the first time in their history after their win on Saturday. They will face one of the giants of non-league football as Bishop Auckland come to Merseyside. Auckland won the FA Amateur Cup ten times and have won the Northern League a record 18 times. They are currently top of the league and aiming for a 19th title. They are also three time FA Trophy Quarter Finalists, although they have never progressed beyond the Third Round of the FA Vase.

Last season saw Droylsden reach the Quarter Finalists and they host Bottesford Town. The Northern Counties East side have reached the Third Round for the first time in their history, and are third in the table at present. They won at Chadderton in the last round.

Holker Old Boys entertain former FA Vase winners North Shields, who overcame Glossop North End in the 2014/15 season. They have had a decent record recently in the Vase, and in three of the last four seasons have reached at least the Fifth Round.

Another big North East name are Shildon who travel to Nelson. Shildon reached the Semi Final in 2012/13, losing 4-3 on aggregate, although they have not reached this stage since the 2020/21 season.  They won 5-0 away at Garstang in the First Qualifying Round.

Yarn & Eaglescliffe are the fourth Northern League side our sides face, but unlike the previous ones they are relatively new to the Non-League System. They have only been in the Northern League for three seasons, winning promotion last season, and this is only their third FA Vase campaign. They have never reached this round before. They will travel to Thornton Cleveleys having beaten Fulwood Amateurs in the First Round.

The final side are Bilston Town who reached the Fifth Round last season. They host Sherwood Colliery who play in the United Counties League Premier Division and are currently in 7th place. The Fourth Round is their previous best, that being last season when they lost at Droylsden, that being the only previous meeting with a NWCFL side.

The draw including our sides can be found below:

THE FA VASE THIRD ROUND PROPER

SATURDAY 28 NOVEMBER 2026

WINNING CLUB TO RECEIVE £1125

LOSING CLUB TO RECEIVE £350

1. Nelson v Shildon

3. Woolton v Bishop Auckland

4. Holker Old Boys v North Shields

6. Droylsden v Bottesford Town

7. Thornton Cleveleys v Yarn & Eaglescliffe

12. Bilston Town v Sherwood Colliery

articles.title: Matchday Preview: Week 14
articles.meta: Fri 30th October 2026 | Match Previews | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Once again, this weekend’s league games threaten to be overshadowed by cup matches, with the Isuzu FA Vase returning on Saturday.

Saturday

Isuzu FA Vase, 2nd Round:

Saturday will see 13 NWCFL teams feature in 13 different Isuzu FA Vase 2nd Round clashes, which means that there is the potential for 13 NWCFL teams to feature in the 3rd Round, should they all come out victorious tomorrow.

The NWCFL teams who will feature in home Vase games include:

That leaves four more teams who will be on the road on Saturday, hoping to take one more step towards Wembley:

Semi-familiar away trips on the cards for Droylsden and Prestwich Heys, who will square off with recent NWCFL member clubs, whilst South Liverpool will go on the road to face the oldest recognised active football club in the English League Pyramid.

Premier Division:

Supplementing the Isuzu FA Vase main course will be a side dish of six Premier Division games on Saturday, all kicking off at 3pm.

With all of the top three all absent from league action, fourth placed Barnoldswick Town will have the chance to close the gap between themselves and top-of-the-table Droylsden to a mere point, should they win at home to 10th placed FC Isle of Man.

Right behind them in fifth are Trafford, who will be afforded the chance to play one of their games in hand that they currently hold over the majority of their contemporaries on Saturday. They will also be at home, with bottom side Abbey hey scheduled to visit Shawe View.

A surprise defeat for Trafford would be music to the ears of eighth placed Irlam, who are currently two points shy of the top five. The right set of results would see them leap into the play-off places this weekend, provided they can see off 11th placed Charnock Richard on home soil.

Virtually the same circumstances apply to Glossop North End as Irlam, with just two goals keeping GNE out of the top eight in the table. Three points would change that on Saturday, with 15th placed Ramsbottom United posing as the SK13 side’s latest hurdle.

Off the back of a Preston derby defeat to Fulwood Amateurs in the Macron Cup last time out, Euxton Villa, in 16th, will be faced with a second local clash on the spin as they welcome Longridge Town to the Jim Fowler Memorial Ground. The visitors are just one point and one place behind their hosts in the table going into this affair.

Just one league position, and a dotted line, separates third bottom Litherland REMYCA from second bottom AFC Liverpool ahead of their meeting at Litherland Sports Park this weekend. The points difference between the two Merseyside outfits threatens to either increase to seven, or drop to just one.

First Division North:

There are as many as eight games scheduled for Saturday from the First Division North.

Leaders Maghull are in serious danger of, at least temporarily, conceding their spot at the top of the tree on Saturday. Just a point behind them and with a league game on the cards this weekend are Cammell Laird 1907, who will host 17th placed Maine Road at the OWS Engineering LTD Stadium.

Flixton are one of two NWCFL newcomers for the season that have set up shop in the top five from their first 15 league games. If they want to maintain that status for Halloween, they will need to put 15th placed Ashton Athletic to the sword on Saturday at Valley Road.

The other side riding high in their debut NWCFL campaign, to the point where the play-offs currently look like a distinct possibility, are fifth placed Halewood Apollo. The 12-year-old club are hoping to recover from their 8-1 defeat in the Macron Cup last Friday with maximum points away at winless bottom side Uppermill.

Defeats for either of the newbies would leave the door ajar for Darwen FC to sneak into the top five, with the Salmoners currently sitting a point behind the play-off spots. They will contest a home game on Saturday, welcoming fifth bottom AFC Knowsley to the Multevo Group Anchor Ground.

Bacup Borough, currently 14th, and Colne, currently seventh, are just three points apart from one another in the standings, and they will play each other on Saturday at the former’s Brian Boys West View Stadium. A home victory would close a wide gap in the mid-table mix.

Fulwood Amateurs upset the on-paper odds last time out with a 4-1 victory against Premier Division Euxton Villa in the Macron Cup. Back in First Division North action, they will hope to carry that momentum into their away fixture against 11th placed Ashton Town.

The right set of results this weekend could afford 10th placed Ashville the opportunity to advance three places in the league standings, and to close the gap between themselves and the top five to just three points. To do that, though, they’ll need to fork out a home win against 16th placed Steeton.

Squires Gate have been given a golden opportunity this weekend to distance themselves from the drop zone. They are currently outside of the bottom three by just a point, but have a game in hand on all three sides below them, and neither Garstang nor AFC Blackpool – the two sides directly beneath them – will feature on Saturday. The catch? They’ll need to beat 12th placed Daisy Hill at home to realise this chance.

First Division South:

Even with one pre-announced postponement, there are eight more league games coming your way from the First Division South on Saturday.

With their two closest challengers in FA Vase action on Saturday, league leaders Sandbach United will have the chance to increase their cushion at the top to a whopping seven points with a win this weekend. They will be on the road to the Theatre of Jockeys to face 11th placed Dawley Town.

Stafford Town are the next best-placed team in league action on Saturday, and a win would see them rise from fourth to second in the standings. Their opponents at Evans Park will be a vengeful Telford Town side, who will be hoping for retribution from an 11-0 defeat suffered on Monday.

Eccleshall currently round out the top five on goal difference alone, helped in part by being the winning team in that 11-0 fixture earlier this week. Victory, and their closest challengers failing to win by six more goals than they can manage, would see them maintain their top five status for Halloweekend as they welcome 15th placed Shawbury United to the Stoke Signage Stadium.

Those closest challengers are Wolverhampton Casuals, who will be hoping for a slip up from their foes as they ready themselves for a home game on Saturday. Allscott Heath will be the visitors to Brinsford Stadium, and they will go into the game just two places worse off than their hosts in the standings.

Barnton are the team situated between Wolverhampton Casuals and Allscott Heath in the league right now, and they will fancy themselves as play-off contenders as October becomes November. They will travel to the Trentham Foods Stadium this weekend to face 12th placed Foley Meir, as they look to keep the pressure on the top six.

Church Lane will host a mid-table clash this Saturday as ninth placed home side New Mills welcome 13th placed NWCFL debutants Wednesfield Community for a clash between sides separated by more places than points in the league table.

Cheadle Heath Nomads have played more league games than any other side in the First Division South so far this season, and won’t be slowing their role this weekend, either. They will be the home side on Saturday at the Ideal Building Systems Stadium, with 14th placed Brereton Social playing the visitors.

There is a decently healthy five-point separating the three sides inside the drop zone in the South from the rest of the division at this early-to-middle stage of the campaign. The two teams directly above the bottom three will meet one another on Saturday at the Balufab Stadium, with fifth bottom Market Drayton Town hosting fourth bottom Crewe.

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 13
articles.meta: Thu 29th October 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. Winter is coming

Storm Boelo made far too many headlines last weekend, and unfortunately, it had a direct impact on many of the NWCFL matches that were scheduled on Saturday.

The Macron Cup was hit the hardest, with seven postponements coming because of waterlogged pitches throughout the North West, and another four to speak of from league games. Despite the weather in general getting colder and drizzlier, hopefully this is not a sign of things to come as October becomes November and we move into the festive period.

2. Speaking of the Macron Cup…

Dreadful weather be damned! There was still plenty of action that took place on Saturday in the cup, and plenty more in rearranged fixtures that came on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Choice cuts include Burscough’s statement 8-1 win against Halewood Apollo on Friday night; FC Isle of Man turning a 2-0 deficit into a 3-2 victory against Maghull; Wolverhampton Casuals netting a 93rd minute winner in a 3-2 win against Crewe; Fulwood Amateurs upsetting Euxton Villa with a 4-1 win in a Preston derby of sorts; and Prestwich Heys conceding an 89th minute equaliser before scoring a 90th minute winner against New Mills. Some games might’ve been delayed, but more of them delivered!

3. Droylsden back on top in the Prem

Away from the Macron Cup, there were three Premier Division matches that were scheduled for Saturday (one of them was postponed thanks to Mother Nature – apologies, Longridge Town and Trafford).

Thankfully for Droylsden, their pencilled-in home game against Glossop North End withstood the wrath of the weather to go the full 90 minutes, and maximum points for the Bloods have taken them back to the top of the table in the absence of a league game for previous leaders Nelson. They’re in the hot seat for now, but their closest challengers do have a game in hand, so watch this space!

4. Eleventh heaven for Eccleshall

Last week, Widnes Town and Dawley Town played out an 11-goal thriller at the Marine Travel Arena, and the game earned its own separate entry into this list. Amazingly, Monday saw the First Division South brandish another game that featured 11 goals, but this one told an entirely different story.

Prior to this week, Eccleshall’s biggest ever win since joining the NWCFL was a 9-0 home victory over Ellesmere Rangers in August of 2019. Seven years later, and they’ve joined the elusive “double-figure winning margin” ranks by putting Telford Town to the sword in an 11-0 win. And they did that away from home, just for good measure!

5. Four-midable Darr and Parker

When one team scores 11 goals in a single match, to hear that one of their players scored four all on their own doesn’t sound all that surprising. Still, you’ve got to be in the right place at the right time, and Eccleshall’s Nicky Parker frequently was on Monday, going one better than a hat-trick as his side ran riot at Telford.

Perhaps more surprising was that Charnock Richard, playing last night in a rearranged Macron Cup fixture from the weekend, also had one of their own score four in a game. The ever-reliable Jordan Darr had bagged a hat-trick by the hour mark of his side’s eventual 5-0 win over Bacup Borough away from home, scoring his fourth in the last three minutes of the game to put the cherry on the icing on the cake.

articles.title: Irlam - PST Sport Premier Division Club of the Month
articles.meta: Thu 29th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Irlam have been presented with their PST Sport Club of the Month award for September 2026. League Director Ian Williams made his way to Tuesday's Macron Cup game at home to Barnton where he is pictured presenting the framed certificate to Club Capyain Jacob Holt.

After winning their final game of August, Irlam went on a great run in September with five wins coming from their five matches. Four of these victories came in the Premier Division whilst they also progressed through to the next round of the Macron Cup. They scored 12 goals and conceded just three, whilst they also registered three clean sheets.

The first game in September for Irlam was at home to Longridge Town. They took an early lead through Luke Mann however by half time Longridge had gained the lead with goals from Josh Ashe and Oliver Hodgson. Irlam equalised 20 minutes into the second half through Jacob Holt, with Daniel Dolling putting them ahead ten minutes later. Dolling then hit another with five minutes remaining to give Irlam a 4-2 win.

Next was a home game against last seasons runners-up Ramsbottom United. After a goalless first half, Jack Mitchell put them ahead ten minutes into the second half before Millen Brown added a second in the last minute to record a 2-0 win.

The third game was a trip to Abbey Hey with Irlam taking the lead just before the half hour through Daragh Mulcahy. They added a second goal three minutes into the second half through Abubakar Muhamme, with Omogbolahan Solarin pulling one back midway through the half with 2-1 the final score.

The final league game of the month was a trip to Glossop North End with Irlam running out 3-0 winners. Daniel Dolling opened the scoring on 11 minutes with Ross Davidson doubling the lead on the stroke of halftime. Dolling scored his second of the game five minutes from time to record a convincing win.

The last game of the month was also against Glossop in the Macron Cup. This time it was at Irlam and was much closer with Jack Mitchell scoring the only goal of the game with 15 minutes remaining.

Burscough also had a strong month as did Nelson and Droylsden, but none could match Irlams perfect record.

Total Games played in the Month: 5Total Points won in the Month: 17Average: 3.40

First Division North - Flixton

Club of the Month in the First Division North is Flixton, who like Irlam had a perfect month of five wins from five games.

Their first month back in the NWCFL saw mixed results as they got to terms with the league, but September saw 16 goals scored in the five games with just three conceded. They also kept two clean sheets.

The first game in September was at home to Steeton with Nathan storton giving the visitors the lead just before the half hour. Flixton will level by a half-time though through a Cian Donohue goal with Donohue putting Flixton ahead in the first minute of the second half. Three minutes later Aaron Dwyer added a third with 3-1 the final score.

The next game also finished 3-1 away at Ashton Athletic however it was not a foregone conclusion for much of the match. Ashley Cata put Flixton ahead on 18 minutes with Ashton levelling 17 minutes from time through Josh Brierley. It wasn't until the 88th minute that Flixton regain the lead through Aaron Dwyer with Benni Smalls-Braithwaite adding another in stoppage time.

Next was Woolton at home with Uche Chinohso Eze giving Flixton the lead on 13 minutes. Three minutes later it was two through Lewis-Simon Byrne, with Byrne adding another just before half time. He then completed his hat-trick on 66 minutes to give his side a 4-0 victory.

Lewis-Simon Byrne hit several hat-tricks last season as he scored 63 goals for Chadderton, and he made it successive hat tricks in the next game as Flixton won 3-1 at Garstang. Byrne's three goals all came in the second half with Luke Draysey scoring a consolation for the home side in stoppage time.

The final game saw Uppermill visit Valley Road with an in form Flixton winning 4-0. Benni Smalls-Braithwaite put them ahead after just six minutes with Kieron Molloy adding second on 27 minutes. Smalls-Braithwaite grabbed his second of the game with eight minutes remaining before completing his hat-trick from the penalty spot in stoppage time.

Thornton Cleveleys also had a good month with five just one loss in their seven games, with Maghull, Colne and Woolton also doing well.

Total Games played in the Month: 5Total Points won in the Month: 18Average: 3.60

First Division South - Bilston Town

The winner of the Club of the Month in the First Division South are Bilston Town. Newcomers to the league this season, they have had an impressive start and sit in the play-off positions at present with games in hand on those above them.

They played four games in the month and were unbeaten, with three of those being victories in which they kept a clean sheet and the other a thrilling draw. They scored 15 goals and conceded just three.

The first game came away at Wolverhampton Casuals where they trailed to a Kieran Cook goal after 17 minutes. Callum Bright levelled just after the half hour only for Cook to restore Wolves lead before half time. Cook then made it 3-1 ten minutes into the second half with Harry Dixon pulling one back on 66 minutes. Bilston levelled with seven minutes remaining through Sam Cudjoe Yankson with the game ending 3-3.

Widnes Town were up next at home with Bilston putting in their most dominant performance of the season to record a 7-0 win. Jordan Crump put Bilston ahead on 14 minutes with Harry Dixon adding another ten minutes later. Ben Priest made it three just before the break with the game over as a contest in a blistering spell at the start of the second half. Nathaniel Hewett scored two minutes into the half before Crump got his second to make it five goals just two minutes later. Dixon made it six just 60 seconds later with Callum Bright adding the seventh just before the hour.

Bilston have lost just once in the league this season, that coming in the first midweek of the season, and they made it six games unbeaten with a 3-0 home win over Market Drayton Town. Harry Dixon put Bilston ahead in the very first minute of the game, but we had to wait until four minutes into the second half for the next goal when Jordan Crump doubled the lead. Darragh Bustin rounded off the scoring with the third midway through the half.

The fourth and final game of the month saw them travel to Stafford Town in the Macron Cup, and they progressed to the next round with a 2-0 win. Nathan Guest opened the scoring on 36 minutes with Harry Dixon adding the second a minute before the break.

Bilston just edged out Wolverhampton Casuals who had two wins and two draws in the month. Barnton, Foley Meir and Sandbach all had an unbeaten month also but draws hindered them.

Total Games played in the Month: 4Total Points won in the Month: 12Average: 3.00

Congratulations to all of the winners.

articles.title: Elliot Wynne - Premier Division Goalkeeper of the Month

articles.title: Isuzu FA Vase Second Round Proper Draw
articles.meta: Mon 12th October 2026 | FA Challenge Vase | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
The FA have today released the draw details for the Second Round Proper of the 2026/27 FA Vase.

Sixty of our member Clubs have entered this year's competition and 17 will be playing in this round. A further five clubs - Bilston Town, Chadderton, Droylsden, Nelson and South Liverpool - will enter at the Second Round after gaining exemption by reaching the Fourth Round last season.

There is chance for a lot of sides to progress with just three all-NWCFL ties. There is a cracking all-First Division North tie as Maghull host Colne, whilst another all-North tie will see Woolton host Ashville. The third is an all-Premier Division tie with Charnock Richard hosting Prestwich Heys.

There are four opponents who will be facing NWCFL sides for the very first time. Atherton LR will welcome Field Olympic who are playing their first season in the National League System after winning the West Yorkshire League last season. They have started the season well and are in third position in the Northern Counties East First Division.

Darlington Town stepped up to the Northern League two years ago to the Northern League, and they travel to FC St Helens who ran out 9-0 winners on Saturday in their FA Vase tie. Darlington currently sit 12th in the Second Division of the Northern League.

The third is Southwell City who play in the First Division of the United Counties League. Southwell is between Nottingham and Lincoln and they travel across to Wolverhampton Casuals. Southwell have also started well and sit in third place in their league.

The final one is Moulton, probably the furthest side any of our sides have ever faced in the First Round of this competition. Moulton are in the Premier Division South of the United Counies League in 13th place at present. They are between Northampton and Kettering and will welcome AFC Bridgnorth, a four hour, 187-mile round trip for our First Division North leaders.

Other ties see Ramsbottom United also face United Counties League opponents as they travel to the World's Oldest Football Club when they make the trip to Sheffield. Foley Meir's reward for reaching this round for the first time is a home tie with Ashby Ivanhoe. And Thornton Cleveleys, another who are in this round for the first time, will host Northern Counties East side Albion Sports.

articles.title: Barney Wiggin - First Division North Player of the Month
articles.meta: Tue 27th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Barney Wiggin has been presented with his First Division North Player of the Month award for September 2026. League Committee Member Craig Buxton popped along to Colne's home game with Ashton Town on Saturday and is pictured presenting Barney with his award.

Barney came through the ranks at FC Halifax Town before switching to Colne at the start of last season which is his first senior club. He soon established himself as a key member of the team and has really kicked on this season. This is the first time Barney has won this award.

September saw Barney play in all eight games that Colne played. He found the net in six of those games, scoring nine goals in total. He hit the only goal in the opening game against Bacup before scoring the second in a 2-0 win at Squires Gate. He also won Man of the Match in that game. The highlight of the month came as Colne thrashed Darwen 6-0, Barney getting a hat-trick as well as winning Man of the Match.

He scored in the 2-0 win at Tow Law Town in the FA Vase and then the equaliser at home to Holker Old Boys in a 1-1 draw. Barney picked up his third Man of the Match in that game also. He also found the net twice against Bamber Bridge in Colne's 4-3 loss in the Lancashire Trophy.

Congratulations to Barney on a fine month.

articles.title: Harry Turner - First Division North Goalkeeper of the Month
articles.meta: Tue 27th October 2026 | League Awards | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
Harry Turner has been presented with his paxsport Goalkeeper of the Month award for September 2026. The Colne goalkeeper was presented with his award prior to Saturday's game with Ashton Town by League Committee Member Craig Buxton.

Harry has a lot of experience playing in the NWCFL having represented Bacup Borough for a number of seasons as well as spells at Darwen, Barnoldswick Town, Ashton Athletic and West Didsbury and Chorlton. He was at Fleetwood Town as a youngster and has also played in Sweden. He signed for Colne at the start of last season.

It has been an exceptional month for Harry in September. He played in all eight games that his side played, helping them to victory in five of them. Those wins, which came at home to Bacup Borough and Darwen, as well as away at Squires Gate, Daisy Hill and Tow Law Town, saw Harry keep five clean sheets.

Across the eight games, he only conceded ten goals, with four coming at the hands of Northern Premier League side Bamber Bridge in the Lancashire Challenge Trophy.

Congratulations to Harry for his performances in the month!

articles.title: Week 13: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Tue 27th October 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
With the Macron Cup dominating the headlines in the NWCFL this past weekend, it only made sense to reach out to some of the competition's biggest winners from the weekend for their post-match thoughts.

One of those big winners were FC Isle of Man, who have progressed to the second round in their first ever season competing in the Macron Cup. Following their 3-2 home win against Maghull, gaffer Lee Dixon said: "If ever there was a game of two halves, this was it.

"Maghull were magnificent in the first 45 minutes and showed exactly why they are top of their league. In the second half, after a tough conversation at half-time, our fast start really shook them and knocked the wind out of their sails.

"I thought my players' response, and their quality and energy in the second half showed why we've been so competitive this season against most of the big teams in our league. All in all it was a great game of football for everyone involved, played with brilliant spirit in tough conditions.

"I was really proud of the fight back from the players to secure a great victory."

Like the Ravens, Barnoldswick Town are another Premier Division side who put adversaries from the First Division North to the sword on Saturday. They beat Darwen FC 3-0 at home, following which, joint-manager Gerry Harrison said: "Having turned up at the ground not knowing what to expect, it was a pleasant surprise to see the pitch in good condition - credit has to go to all concerned in preparing the pitch.

"Our instructions to the team, due to the horrendous conditions, was that there will be mistakes made by both teams and that we should try to limit our mistakes made in crucial areas.

"The game started and both teams looked up for it and it was pretty even. After about 10 minutes, Darwen went down to 10 men and a penalty was conceded, which we scored from. On reflection, the turning point was the sending off, as it allowed us to be more patient with the ball.

"We scored another in the first half and went into the break 2-0 up. In the second half we created a lot of chances, but credit has to go to Darwen, who showed themselves to be a very good side. They missed a penalty, forcing made our keeper make a great save at 2-0.

"A third goal was added to make it 3-0, which enabled us to see the game out. Overall, I would say that we made the least mistakes, and credit must go to both teams for their heart in the horrendous conditions."

Another side that put their names in the hat for the next round of the Macron Cup were First Division North outfit Eccleshall. They won 4-1 away from home to see off Wednesfield Community. After the whistle, manager Danny Glover called the win: "A great performance.

"Wednesfield are a side who got the better of us in the league last month, so we were determined to put things right from the start.

"I gave opportunities to a few lads who have been patiently waiting for their chance, and they certainly didn’t disappoint. They all put in a fantastic shift, and we ran out comfortable winners in the end, showing real character to battle through a spell with 10 men and even going down to nine at one point.

"I'm very proud of the performance, the attitude and the togetherness shown by the group.

"A big thank you must go to Wednesfield and their staff for getting the game on in some tricky weather conditions."

There was league action to speak of away from the Macron Cup on Saturday. In the Premier Division, Droylsden retook top spot in the standings with a 3-1 home victory over Glossop North End, maintaining their unbeaten home record in the league this season as a consequence.

After the win, manager Dave Pace kept it short and sweet with his thoughts: "I was very pleased with the character we showed. Especially after down to ten men with forty minutes to go, it was a great performance from everyone involved."

In the First Division North, maximum points were also secured for mid-table Colne, who completed a 3-1 turnaround to see off Ashton Town. Gaffer Andy Mapperson said after full time that: "It was nice to finally be back at home after seven consecutive away games.

"The weather was the worst I've seen on a football pitch for as long as I can remember and proved problematic for both sides. But we stuck to the game plan and played some great football at times, and made sure the weather never became an excuse.

"A massive shoutout must go to groundsman Richard and our other groundstaff for doing a great job to ensure the game was on, and to ensure that it went the full 90 minutes."

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 11
articles.meta: Thu 15th October 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
Another week, another series of matches from the NWCFL. Let's run through the best and worst of what the last week has had to offer.

1. Wembley is still a possibility

Despite Trafford’s defeat in the FA Cup last week meaning that there are no more NWCFL sides left in the competition, there’s still the prospect of a Wembley bow for the remaining ten teams from the league in the Isuzu FA Vase.

A handful of first round matches took place this past Saturday, with all of Prestwich Heys, FC St Helens, Holker Old Boys, Maghull, AFC Bridgnorth, Burscough, Woolton, Atherton LR and Thornton Cleveleys coming away with a victory – the final two teams on that list even braved a penalty shootout to get their names in the hat for the Second Round. And on top of that, both Droylsden and Bilston Town received byes into the second round proper for this season!

2. AFC Liverpool are on the board

It has taken 12 games, but last season’s Macron Cup winners AFC Liverpool have finally picked up their first point of the league season this past Saturday. They have now halved the deficit between themselves and the rest of the division, with Abbey Hey, directly above them. Currently sitting on two points.

The end of their winless streak came on home soil, just to make it even sweeter, and it came via a 93rd minute equaliser from Christopher Happi-Fankam in a 3-3 comeback draw against high-flying Trafford. Is this finally a platform for Jack Edwards men to build the rest of their season upon?

3. A four-midable Kuda performance

Barnoldswick Town piled more misery onto second-bottom Abbey hey on Saturday, putting them to the sword in a 5-2 victory at the Silentnight Stadium. Looking purely at the numbers, the absence of Kuda Chingwaro from Barlick’s starting XI would’ve seen Abbey Hey pick up maximum points.

Instead, the hosts’ number 11 was at the centre of nearly everything positive that was put together by Barnoldswick whenever they went on the attack. He bagged all but one of their five on the day, and stands out from the weekend’s other hat-trick heroes with his four-goal haul.

4. Five stars all around in the North in midweek

Tuesday evening brought a healthy serving of NWCFL action, and if you were fortunate enough to watch a game from the First Division North that night, odds are your ticket was worth the money.

Flixton’s and Colne’s goalless draw to one side, every other match from the North saw one team score at least five goals. Halewood Apollo were the victors in a 5-2 away game against AFC Knowsley; Fulwood Amateurs took down Ashton Athletic on home soil by the same scoreline; and Steeton went one better, winning by four in a 5-1 dressing down of bottom side Uppermill – don’t blink, or you’ll miss something.

5. Bilston Town one blip from perfection

Much has been made already this season of First Division South debutants AFC Bridgnorth, who had maintained the longest unbeaten run in the NWCFL from the start of the league season until mid-to-late September. One of the teams they defeated early on in that run were fellow newcomers Bilston Town, who have since picked themselves up, dusted themselves off, and have not looked back.

Dave King’s side won at home yesterday and on Saturday to extend their winning streak to six games in all competitions, and their unbeaten run to 10 games in all competitions. This blazing run of form has meant that the club are now second in the division, behind only Sandbach United, who they will go on the road to face this coming weekend – a win would send them top!

articles.title: Week 12: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Mon 19th October 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
This weekend saw a plethora of league games from the NWCFL end as high-scoring affairs.

There's nowhere better start than towards the top of the tree in the Premier Division, where promotion hopefuls Burscough won 5-2 on away soil this weekend against Longridge Town. Following the win, satisfied gaffer Phil Stafford said: “another three points is all that matters today.

“It was probably our worst first half performance of the season, but we echoed that with our best second half performance. We knew Longridge posed a serious threat going forward and they proved that again today.

“The biggest positive for me and the group is that they never quit - they don’t know when they are beat. That’s a sign of a good side, and once again, all 16 lads in the squad produced a great second half performance.”

They weren’t the biggest winners in the Premier Division this past weekend, however. That distinction goes to Trafford, who put South Liverpool to the sword in a 6-1 win in front of a home crowd on Saturday. After full time, manager Tom Baker told the club media: “I think the three points and the win was the really important thing, after a few games without a win.

“I think it’s good that we’ve scored so many goals towards the end after threatening to for quite a few games, and in general this season.

“How we went in at 2-1 up at half time, I don’t know. We had countless chances in the first half. The goal that we gave away was very sloppy, but, with all due respect to our opponents, we could’ve been four or five up by half time.

“We started a bit like that in the second half, but that third goal gave us confidence, and we looked really clinical within the last 25 to 20 minutes. That’s the way it goes sometimes, but sometimes it doesn’t go like that.

“They [South Liverpool] are a good team – they’re young, energetic, they had quality in certain areas, they were a threat, but the important thing today was getting the three points, and we’ve got that.”

In the First Division North, new boys and former relegation zone occupiers AFC Knowsley have shot out of the bottom three as of this weekend, with an emphatic 4-0 win over Squires Gate. After the whistle, manager David Platt said: “Following a couple of tough games, we needed a reaction against a team who are close to us in the league.

“Whilst Squires Gate were unlucky with an early injury and sending off, we created those situations with quick, direct play, and we got into good positions early.

“I’m made up with the attitude shown by the lads after a tough run, and my only real criticism is that we were a bit wasteful in front of goal - we really should have scored more.

“Credit to Squires Gate, who worked hard and were good on the ball, even when they were a man down.”

Also in the North, Ashton Athletic recorded a perfect result on paper with the home crowd at Brocstedes Park in their corner. They welcomed Holker Old Boys, and sent their visitors packing with a 3-0 victory after 90 minutes, following which, manager Jay Foulds said: "It was great to get back to winning ways with such a solid victory.

To the South, and another side that were the beneficiaries of a big win and clean sheet were Allscott Heath. They put six past Foley Meir without reply at the Peter Ford Stadium in a game that also featured a Ben Davies hat-trick. Following the win, manager Harvinder Singh said: “Our lads were dangerous from the first minute.

“Our top goalscorer, Ben Davies, put the first one in the back of the net within five minutes. From there, we proceeded to play fast, attacking and positive football, and Ben scored his second after 30 minutes, and our skipper, Jacob Welch, added a third on the stroke of half time.

“The second half was more of the same and the lads were tasked with a job to kill the game. Their motivation was clear – to become the top scorers in the league. The Monners delivered just that as we end the weekend by reaching 39 with our goal tally for the season.”

Finally, in what was almost certainly the game of the weekend, Dawley Town emerged victorious from an absolute war away from home against Widnes Town.

The Jockeys came away with maximum points from a 6-5 barnstormer of a game, following which, joint-gaffer Tom White simply said: “What a game for the neutral - not for a manager though!

“I think I felt every emotion possible during those 90 minutes! But we got the job done. That's a massive three points for us, and the lads showed true Dawley spirit and never gave up throughout.

“Hopefully we can kick on now and keep picking up points. Our togetherness is key - UP THE JOCKEYS!”
